problem: The trap says 'U-Net and FCN skip connections concatenate channels (64 + 64 = 128)'. The original FCN fuses its coarse score map with the earlier, finer prediction by element-wise addition, not concatenation. Only U-Net concatenates. The trap therefore contradicts Section 1, which correctly allows 'add it or concatenate it', and it would make students write the wrong fusion rule for FCN.
fix: U-Net skips concatenate channels (64 + 64 = 128). FCN skips add tensors of equal shape: the 2× upsampled coarse score map is summed with the score map predicted from the earlier layer. ResNet shortcuts also add tensors of equal shape.

where: Section 2 (ROIPool sentence) and Quiz Q6 answer
problem: 'Shifting features by up to one pixel' is measured on the feature map, not on the image. At stride 16 one feature-map pixel is 16 image pixels, so the misalignment a student pictures is wrong.
fix: Say: ROIPool rounds proposal coordinates and bin edges to the integer feature-map grid, so the pooled features can be off by up to one feature-map pixel — several image pixels at stride 16 — and a pixel-accurate mask shows that shift.
